ACTION: Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-skills/references/claude-code.md

The likely cause is the size of the skill listing, not `api-naming` itself. Before you can type anything, the model sees only each skill's name and `description`. Claude Code puts that listing under a budget. With about 150 skills installed, mostly from three plugins, the listing is probably over budget, and that's what `/doctor` is warning about. When the listing overflows, Claude Code drops or shortens some descriptions. If `api-naming` lost its description, the model sees its name with nothing saying when to use it, so it stops triggering on its own. Typing `/api-naming` still works because that loads the skill by name and never consults the listing. This also explains why it broke last week even though nobody edited it: a plugin install or update most likely pushed the total over the budget.

Your description is fine. At 410 characters it's under the 1024 cap and the ~500 target, and it starts with "Use when". A rewrite won't help unless it makes the description survive whatever rule Claude Code uses to choose what to drop.

I'm reading `references/claude-code.md` now. It documents exactly how Claude Code's listing drops descriptions, including which skills lose theirs first and whether the cut is by order, by length or by source. I'll confirm the mechanism there before recommending a specific change.

The fix will probably be one or more of these, depending on what that file says:

1. **Shrink the listing.** Disable or uninstall the plugin skills you don't use. This is usually the biggest win, and it helps every skill, not just `api-naming`.
2. **Stop auto-triggering skills that are only ever typed.** Any skill you always run by slash command can be set to `disable-model-invocation: true`. It stays available as `/name` but stops taking up listing budget.
3. **Trim long plugin descriptions** where you control them, so the total fits.

Could you paste the full `/doctor` warning? It should say how far over the budget you are, and that tells us how much has to go.
